# The billion-row problem

Given a text file where every line is `station;temperature` (e.g. `Hamburg;12.0`),
print the **min / mean / max temperature per station**.

The original challenge (Gunnar Morling's "1BRC", January 2024) used
**1,000,000,000 rows (~13 GB)**. Our generated file starts at 1M rows so it runs
in seconds; scale up as far as your laptop allows.

```
python3 generate_data.py            # 1M rows
python3 naive.py                    # attempt 1: load everything
python3 lazy.py                     # attempt 2: generator pipeline
python3 lazy_binary.py              # attempt 3: a 'clever' tweak -- is it actually faster?
```

Try bigger: `python3 generate_data.py 10000000`, then re-run all three and
compare time AND peak memory. Watch which number grows with the file size.

`measurements.txt` is generated by `generate_data.py`
